cards.explanation: The answer is My wrath. The LORD says, "Woe to Assyria, the rod of My anger; the staff in their hands is My wrath." (Isaiah 10:5) So Assyria is the rod, and the staff in their hands is His wrath. That's a whole lot of heat packed into one verse, friends.

The answer is True. The LORD says He'll send Assyria against a godless nation "…to take spoils and seize plunder…" (Isaiah 10:6) Spoils and plunder are what an army carries off after winning. So the verse spells out exactly what Assyria is sent to do, friends.

The answer is to destroy and cut off many nations. The text says it's in his heart "…to destroy and cut off many nations." (Isaiah 10:7) God sends him on one mission, but Assyria is carrying a bigger plan in his own heart. That's a man who got handed a job and decided to freelance, friends.

The answer is False. He pairs cities up: "Is not Calno like Carchemish? Is not Hamath like Arpad? Is not Samaria like Damascus?" (Isaiah 10:9) The point is that they're alike, not that one is tougher to take. I think he's bragging that none of them is any different from the next, friends.

The answer is their images. Assyria says his hand seized "…the idolatrous kingdoms whose images surpassed those of Jerusalem and Samaria…" (Isaiah 10:10) Images are idols, and he says theirs surpassed the ones in those two cities. So his brag is about taking kingdoms whose idols surpassed these, bakers.
The answer is Jerusalem. He asks, "…will I not also do to Jerusalem and her idols?" (Isaiah 10:11) He's already done it to Samaria and its idols. In his mind, Jerusalem is next on the list, friends.

The answer is arrogant. The Lord says, "I will punish the king of Assyria for the fruit of his arrogant heart and the proud look in his eyes." (Isaiah 10:12) Arrogant heart and proud eyes. That's a whole attitude you can see from across the room, bakers.

The answer is False. The king says, "By the strength of my hand I have done this, and by my wisdom, for I am clever." (Isaiah 10:13) He credits his own hand and his own wisdom. The LORD doesn't get a mention in his boast, friends.

The answer is abandoned eggs. The king says, "Like one gathering abandoned eggs, I gathered all the earth." (Isaiah 10:14) Right after that, he adds that no wing fluttered and no beak opened or chirped. He's picturing it as easy as picking up eggs nobody is guarding, bakers.

The answer is True. The passage asks, "Does an axe raise itself above the one who swings it? Does a saw boast over him who saws with it?" (Isaiah 10:15) An axe doesn't lift itself over the person swinging it. The expected answer is no, and that's the whole point against Assyria's bragging, friends.

The answer is fire. The text says, "And the Light of Israel will become a fire, and its Holy One a flame." (Isaiah 10:17) Fire and flame, right in the same line. That's a big change for a light, friends.
The answer is False. Isaiah 10:17 says, "In a single day it will burn and devour Assyria’s thorns and thistles." Years don't come into it. One day, and the thorns and thistles are gone, friends.

The answer is so few a child could count them. The passage says, "The remaining trees of its forests will be so few that a child could count them." (Isaiah 10:19) Forests that were once full of splendor, and now a child can count what's left. Think about how short that count would be, friends.
